summary: Discovery + POC scoping to size workload and define success criteria for Horizon Payments. Key goals: define QPS/concurrency targets, token distribution, benchmark plan, timeline and security requirements. POC planned for 4 weeks with benchmark runs on hosted and Dedicated variants.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-02-10
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Horizon Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Priya Rao (Security)

Summary:
Redwood and Horizon discussed POC scope focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Horizon will provide sample traffic; Redwood will run benchmarks (hosted & dedicated) and compare latency/cost. Success criteria include p95 latency, token-accuracy/regression limits, and cost per 1M tokens threshold. Timeline target: kickoff next week, 3-4 week POC with checkpoints.

Topics:
- Current traffic patterns & QPS targets
- Concurrency and burst behavior
- Input/output token distribution and percentiles
- Benchmarks (models, hardware, metrics)
- Security & data residency requirements
- Success criteria and go/no-go thresholds
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intro, I'm Sofia with Redwood, this is Dan our SE. Maya, do you want to start with the high level use case?
00:10 Maya: Yeah thanks Sofia. We're looking to add an LLM layer for real-time customer support routing and merchant insights. Latency is pretty important, most flows need human-comparable response times, so 200 to 500 ms ballpark ideally.
00:25 Daniel: Right, that's helpful. Can you share current QPS and concurrency numbers so we can size? Also typical input token lengths?
00:33 Liam: Sure, on peak we see around 10 QPS sustained, with spikes up to ~60 QPS for short bursts. Concurrency - the app maintains about 40 to 60 concurrent sessions during peaks. For tokens, median user message is ~90 to 140 tokens, responses average 30 to 60 tokens. There's also longer analytic jobs that produce 500-2k tokens but they are off-peak.
00:56 Sofia: OK so for the POC we should model both the interactive path and the heavy batch analytic path. For interactive, we'll focus on 10 QPS steady state, 60 QPS bursts, concurrency 50. For benching we'll also run a 5 QPS analytics workload with large outputs.
01:15 Maya: That sounds right. Wanted to confirm accuracy requirements — we need no more than 5% regression on our internal prompts vs current baseline and p95 latency under 400 ms for interactive end-to-end (including network).
01:29 Daniel: On the model side, do you have a preference? We can validate Redwood-verified open models; we can also run trimmed quantized variants on dedicated infra to lower cost.
01:40 Maya: We prefer open models for now, but willing to try a couple variants. Primary is consistency and reproducibility.
01:46 Priya: From security, we need SOC2, data residency for EU merchants, and KMS-integrated key management for any private deployment. Also audit logs for per-request traceability.
01:58 Sofia: Absolutely. We'll include the SOC2 pack and our private deployment docs. For POC we'll run hosted first, and a dedicated run if we see capacity/latency concerns. Does that work?
02:10 Liam: Yes. About benchmarks — what metrics will you provide? We need token-level cost, latency percentiles, throughput, and memory/kv cache behavior.
02:21 Daniel: We'll provide tokenized input/output distributions, per-token latency breakdowns (kernel times, batching overhead), cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated, and recommendations on batching and KV caching. We'll also provide a runbook for reproducing the tests.
02:36 Maya: Timeline — how long for setup and runs?
02:39 Sofia: We can kick off in 1 week after sample data. Initial hosted benchmarks: 3 business days for baseline runs and analysis. Dedicated benchmark + tuning another 5 business days. Total POC 3-4 weeks including check-ins.
02:51 Priya: For dedicated, our procurement needs an estimate of committed capacity and cost per month. Can you provide a sample config? GPU types, counts.
03:02 Daniel: For modeling we'll run H100 and A100 profiles, and also quantized 8-bit runs on T4-like equivalence. For your workload with concurrency 50 and 60 QPS peaks, preliminary ballpark is 2-4 GPUs for dedicated (depending on batching), we'll generate precise numbers after we model token distributions.
03:22 Liam: Can you explain how batching affects latency for short inputs — we're worried about tail latency.
03:27 Daniel: Sure. Continuous batching can increase throughput but might add steady-state latency depending on configured batch windows. We can tune batch size and timeout; for interactive flows we'll use low-latency settings (micro-batches) to keep p95 low. KV cache will give big savings for repeated prefixes which you said you have in session flows.
03:45 Maya: About traffic sample — what format do you need?
03:49 Sofia: CSV with columns: timestamp, route, input_text, expected_response_type, region (optional). If you can provide tokenized lengths even better but we can tokenise. 7 days of traffic preferred.
03:58 Liam: We'll get a scrubbed 7-day sample (no PII) by next Wednesday 2027-02-17.
04:05 Priya: For encryption, we will need your private deployment to support our KMS and not export logs outside our VPC during Dedicated runs.
04:13 Daniel: Noted. We have KMS integrations and options for private control plane; we'll call that out in the security pack.
04:20 Sofia: For success criteria recap — Maya, you said p95 latency < 400ms, accuracy regression <5%, and cost per 1M tokens below your internal threshold (you gave a number last week around $2500)?
04:33 Maya: Yes that aligns. Also minimal operational friction for rollout — we can't have frequent model regressions.
04:39 Sofia: Great. We'll produce a benchmark plan and a proposed config for dedicated. Action items and dates we'll email right after. Any other competitors or existing investments we should be aware of?
04:51 Liam: We're evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI at the API level; we're also testing LocalOps self-host for cost reasons but it's not production-ready.
04:59 Sofia: Got it. We'll include comparative notes.
05:02 Daniel: Quick note — we'll run traffic modeling to produce QPS vs latency curves, token distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) for both input and output, and an estimated cost model per million tokens across target configs.
05:15 Maya: Sounds good. Let's schedule the kickoff next Tuesday and plan the benchmark week.

Recap / Next steps:
- Horizon to send 7 days sample traffic CSV by 2027-02-17 (Liam)
- Redwood to send SOW + POC pricing by 2027-02-15 (Sofia)
- Redwood SE to share benchmark plan + metrics and runbook by 2027-02-16 (Daniel)
- Schedule kickoff meeting for 2027-02-22

Notes on modeling assumptions (verbatim from call):
- Interactive path: steady 10 QPS, bursts to 60 QPS, concurrency ~50
- Tokens: median input 90-140, median output 30-60, analytic path outputs 500-2k tokens
- Targets: p95 < 400ms, accuracy regression <5%, cost per 1M tokens < $2500 (customer threshold)

References shared during call:
- Link: POC SOW template (shared)
- Link: Security pack (SOC2, KMS notes)
- Note: customer will provide scrubbed traffic CSV and an eval prompt set (10-20 prompts) for quality checks

End of transcript.
